phases.name: Re-entry
phases.focus: Rebuild tolerance after the break: light loads, run-walk, technique, shoulder care. Week 4 = baseline tests.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.focus: Volume and aerobic base. First tempo runs. Pike push-ups, pull-up and dip volume. Week 12 = tests.

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Heavier strength (sets of 4 and 3), intervals, wall HSPU negatives, explosive pulls. Week 24 = month-6 checkpoint.

phases.name: Strength
phases.focus: Strength peak #1, muscle-up attempts, full-range wall HSPU, freestanding holds. Week 36 = tests.

phases.name: Hybrid Peak
phases.focus: 5K-specific running, heavy strength kept, freestanding HSPU negatives, dips to 20. Week 48 = tests.

phases.name: Realize
phases.focus: Peak, taper, final tests (week 51) and 5K race, then a recovery week.

One session a day: at the end of your workout, or any time that day. Rest about 1 minute between sets. Squeeze as if stopping urine and holding in gas, without clenching glutes, thighs or abs, and keep breathing. Relax fully between reps. Don't practise by actually stopping urine. Pain or symptoms: see a pelvic-floor physio. REVERSE KEGEL (the 'drop'): lie on your back, knees bent, one hand on your belly. Breathe in slowly so the belly rises; as you breathe out, let the pelvic floor soften and sink, as if your sit bones were moving apart - the feeling when you start to pee. It is a let-go, never a push or strain. Can't feel it? Squeeze gently first, then let go, and keep letting go. Video (pelvic-floor physio Michelle Kenway): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Auca88tmUu8 NHS guide for men, see 'Pelvic floor relaxation': https://royalberkshire.nhs.uk/leaflets/pelvic-floor-strengthening-and-relaxation-exercises-for-men 'Pelvic floor drops' handout (Alberta Health Services): https://cumming.ucalgary.ca/sites/default/files/teams/88/Reverse%20Kegels%20or%20PF_Drops.pdf
